questions.question_text: An open-top cylinder (a base but no lid) has a radius of $6$ cm and a height of $9$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Includes two ends ($2\pi r^{2}$), but the top is open, so only one end counts.
Gives only the curved surface $2\pi rh$ and leaves out the circular base.

questions.solution_text:
An open-top cylinder has one circular base and the curved surface, but no lid.
$A = \pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$
$= \pi(6)^{2} + 2\pi(6)(9)$
$= 36\pi + 108\pi$
$= 144\pi$
$= 452.3893\ldots$
$\approx 452.4\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A pipe is open at both ends. It has a radius of $3$ cm and a length of $25$ cm. Find its surface area in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Adds two circular ends ($2\pi r^{2}$), but a pipe is open at both ends.
Adds one circular end, but both ends of a pipe are open.

questions.solution_text:
A pipe open at both ends has only its curved surface.
$A = 2\pi rh$
$= 2\pi(3)(25)$
$= 150\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A closed half-cylinder has a radius of $5$ cm and a length of $8$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Omits the flat rectangular top ($2r \times h$) that the cut exposes.
Uses the full curved surface $2\pi rh$ instead of half of it, $\pi rh$.

questions.solution_text:
A closed half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether), half the curved surface ($\pi rh$), and a flat rectangular top ($2r \times h$).
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh + 2rh$
$= \pi(5)^{2} + \pi(5)(8) + 2(5)(8)$
$= 25\pi + 40\pi + 80$
$= 65\pi + 80$
$= 284.2035\ldots$
$\approx 284.20\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A half-cylinder trough is open along the top. It has a radius of $4$ cm and a length of $9$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Adds a flat rectangular top ($2r \times h$), but the trough is open on top.
Uses the full curved surface $2\pi rh$ instead of half of it, $\pi rh$.

questions.solution_text:
An open-top half-cylinder has two semicircular ends ($\pi r^{2}$ altogether) and half the curved surface ($\pi rh$), but no flat top.
$A = \pi r^{2} + \pi rh$
$= \pi(4)^{2} + \pi(4)(9)$
$= 16\pi + 36\pi$
$= 52\pi$
$= 163.3628\ldots$
$\approx 163.36\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A closed quarter-cylinder has a radius of $5$ cm and a length of $12$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Omits the two flat rectangular faces ($2rh$) exposed by the quarter cut.
Uses half-cylinder amounts ($\pi r^{2}$ and $\pi rh$) instead of quarter amounts.

questions.solution_text:
A closed quarter-cylinder has two quarter-circle ends ($\tfrac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}$ altogether), a quarter of the curved surface ($\tfrac{1}{2}\pi rh$), and two flat rectangular faces ($2rh$).
$A = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\pi rh + 2rh$
$= \frac{1}{2}\pi(5)^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\pi(5)(12) + 2(5)(12)$
$= 12.5\pi + 30\pi + 120$
$= 42.5\pi + 120$
$= 253.5177\ldots$
$\approx 253.52\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: Which expression gives the surface area of a cylinder that is open at one end (it has a base but no lid), with radius $r$ and height $h$?

options.why: Counts two circular ends, but the open top means only one end is present.
Gives only the curved surface and leaves out the circular base.
Halves the curved surface; a full cylinder's curved surface is $2\pi rh$.

questions.solution_text:
A cylinder open at one end keeps one circular base ($\pi r^{2}$) and the full curved surface ($2\pi rh$).
$A = \pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh$

questions.question_text: A semicircular gutter is a half-cylinder open along the top and at both ends. It has a radius of $8$ cm and a length of $50$ cm. Find its surface area, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Uses the full curved surface $2\pi rh$, not the half $\pi rh$ a gutter has.
Adds two semicircular ends, but the gutter is open at both ends.

questions.solution_text:
A gutter open along the top and at both ends has only its curved surface, half a full cylinder's.
$A = \pi rh$
$= \pi(8)(50)$
$= 400\pi$
$= 1256.6370\ldots$
$\approx 1256.6\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A pipe is open at both ends and has a radius of $6$ cm. Its surface area is $180\pi$ cm². Find the length of the pipe.

options.why: Uses $\pi rh$ instead of $2\pi rh$ for a pipe, halving the divisor.
Adds two ends first, treating $180\pi$ as if the pipe were closed.

questions.question_text: An open-top cylinder (a base but no lid) has a radius of $4$ cm. The total of its base and curved surface is $96\pi$ cm². Find the height of the cylinder.

options.why: Subtracts two ends, treating the solid as closed, but the top is open.
Ignores the base entirely, dividing $96\pi$ by just $2\pi r$.
